newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Islamists urge Arabs to cut Israel ties.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Islamists urge Arabs to cut Israel ties.

text.p: Jordan's opposition Islamists on Saturday urged Arab parties to the Middle East peace process to cut links with Israel.

The Islamic Action Front (IAF), Jordan's largest opposition party with 16 seats in the 80-seat parliament, branded as a failure the Middle East peace summit held in Washington after Israeli-Palestinian clashes that killed 73 people.
Jordan's King Hussein attended the summit along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Jordan became the second Arab country after Egypt to sign a peace treaty with the Jewish state. Egypt declined to attend the summit.

The IAF, in a statement, accused Clinton of not exerting pressure on Israel to soften its hardline stances. It described the summit as a U.S. ploy to defuse Palestinian anger against stepped up Israeli moves to "Judaise" Jersualem.

"Stop all forms of dealing with the Zionist enemy and the race to normalise ties, close all embassies and offices that have been opened with the Zionist enemy in our capitals that have defaced the sanctity of our lands," the IAF added.
"What are Arabs and Moslems waiting for after all peaceful paths have closed and all compromise solutions failed?" it said.
The IAF is capitalising on growing doubts among Jordanians about Israel's peace intentions since Netanyahu took office in June.

The party is also playing up popular emotions over the sensitive issue of the Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem and the al-Aqsa Mosque complex, Islam's third holiest site, after Israel opened a second entrance to a tourist tunnel near them.
"Save Jerusalem before al-Aqsa mosque's demolition and the Judaisation of the city, wake up to the dangers of the Zionist plots that aim at us and does not exclude any of us," the IAF said.
